title: Monotonicity of bounded-error space
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a language of binary strings, and $s,s':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ space bounds. Suppose $N$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells on every input and choice word, and for each input there is a time bound by which all branches halt and the probability of outputting the one-bit membership value for $L$ is at least $2/3$. If $s(n)\le s'(n)$ for every $n$, then the same machine satisfies these decision conditions with space bound $s'$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
$N$ satisfies the stated bounded-error decision conditions with space bound $s$
